audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Elihu's justice speech: appeal to wise hearers, quotation/summary of Job, defense of divine justice, impartiality toward rulers and poor, divine seeing, hiddenness, and Elihu's critique of Job. Marked as Elihu's speech, not final theology.

verses.restored: Elihu answered and said:

familiar.text: Furthermore Elihu answered and said,

verses.restored: Hear my words, you wise ones, and give ear to me, you who know.

familiar.text: Hear my words, O ye wise men; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.

verses.restored: For the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.

familiar.text: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.

verses.restored: Let us choose justice for ourselves; let us know among ourselves what is good.

familiar.text: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what is good.

verses.restored: For Job has said, I am righteous, but the Divine has turned aside my justice.

familiar.text: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.

verses.restored: Concerning my justice, should I lie? My wound is incurable though I have no transgression.

familiar.text: Should I lie against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression.

verses.restored: What man is like Job, who drinks mockery like water,

familiar.text: What man is like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water?

verses.restored: who travels in company with workers of harm and walks with wicked people?

familiar.text: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.

verses.restored: For he has said, It profits a strong man nothing to delight in the Divine.

familiar.text: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.

verses.restored: Therefore, hear me, people of heart: far be it from the Divine to do wickedness, and from Shaddai to do injustice.

familiar.text: Therefore hearken unto me ye men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

verses.restored: For he repays a human according to his deed, and according to a person's way he makes it find him.

familiar.text: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.

verses.restored: Surely the Divine does not do wickedness, and Shaddai does not twist justice.

familiar.text: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.

verses.restored: Who appointed the earth to him, and who placed the whole world under him?

familiar.text: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?

verses.restored: If he set his heart upon himself, if he gathered to himself his spirit and breath,

familiar.text: If he set his heart upon man, if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;

verses.restored: all flesh would expire together, and humanity would return to dust.

familiar.text: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.

verses.restored: If you have understanding, hear this; give ear to the sound of my words.

familiar.text: If now thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.

verses.restored: Shall one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the righteous, mighty One?

familiar.text: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?

verses.restored: Who says to a king, Worthless one, and to nobles, Wicked one?

familiar.text: Is it fit to say to a king, Thou art wicked? and to princes, Ye are ungodly?

verses.restored: Who shows no partiality to princes and does not recognize rich more than poor, for they are all the work of his hands?

familiar.text: How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands.

verses.restored: In a moment they die; at midnight people are shaken and pass away, and the mighty are removed without a hand.

familiar.text: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.

verses.restored: For his eyes are on a person's ways, and he sees all his steps.

familiar.text: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.

verses.restored: There is no darkness and no deep shadow where workers of harm may hide themselves.

familiar.text: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

verses.restored: For he does not need to set a time for a person to go before the Divine in judgment.

familiar.text: For he will not lay upon man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.

verses.restored: He breaks mighty ones without searching and sets others in their place.

familiar.text: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.

verses.restored: Therefore he recognizes their works; he overturns them in the night, and they are crushed.

familiar.text: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.

verses.restored: He strikes them as wicked people in a place where others see,

familiar.text: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

verses.restored: because they turned aside from following him and had no insight into any of his ways,

familiar.text: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:

verses.restored: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him, and he heard the cry of the afflicted.

familiar.text: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.

verses.restored: When he gives quiet, who can condemn? When he hides his face, who can behold him, whether over a nation or a human together?

familiar.text: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only:

verses.restored: so that a godless person should not reign, nor be snares for the people.

familiar.text: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.

verses.restored: For has anyone said to the Divine, I have borne chastening; I will not act corruptly?

familiar.text: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:

verses.restored: What I do not see, teach me; if I have done injustice, I will not do it again.

familiar.text: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.

verses.restored: Should he repay on your terms because you reject it? You must choose, not I; so speak what you know.

familiar.text: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.

verses.restored: People of heart will say to me, and a wise man who hears me:

familiar.text: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me.

verses.restored: Job speaks without knowledge, and his words are without insight.

familiar.text: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom.

verses.restored: Would that Job were tested to the end, because of answers like people of harm.

familiar.text: My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men.

verses.restored: For he adds rebellion to his sin; among us he claps his hands and multiplies his words against the Divine.

familiar.text: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.
